canonical_statement.plain_language: Every realized continuation conditions the topology through which subsequent continuation is evaluated. Repeated coherent continuation may reinforce that conditioning by increasing the admissibility of compatible future continuation.
canonical_statement.minimal_statement: Continuation conditions topology; conditioned topology modifies subsequent admissibility.
canonical_statement.strong_form_boundary: Reinforcement requires repeated sufficiently coherent continuation and may be weakened, redirected, erased, or reorganized by other continuations.

core_definitions.continuation: Lawful realization of a distinction condition through an admissible relational boundary without requiring transport of an object or substance.
core_definitions.topology: Present relational organization of basins, boundaries, orientations, and admissible continuation relations; an active conditioning structure rather than passive background geometry.
core_definitions.topological_conditioning: Modification of relational topology by realized continuation such that admissibility, resistance, orientation, or accessibility of subsequent continuation is altered.
core_definitions.continuation_resistance: Relational opposition presented by a boundary or basin configuration to a candidate continuation.
core_definitions.reinforcement: Conditional cumulative strengthening of a topological bias under repeated compatible continuation.
core_definitions.residue: Present topological conditioning produced by prior continuation; not leftover matter, detached history, or deposited substance.

sequence: Candidate continuation encounters an ordered relational boundary.
Admissibility evaluates boundary and neighboring basin resistance.
A satisfied condition realizes continuation without primitive transported identity.
Realized continuation modifies boundary relations, basin accessibility, orientation, resistance, or thresholds.
Subsequent continuation is evaluated against the conditioned topology.
Repeated coherent continuation may deepen or stabilize a compatible pathway.

entities.C_n: Realized continuation at ordinal position n
entities.A_T: Admissibility relation induced by topology T

formal_candidate.admissibility_rule: C_(n+1) is evaluated under A_(T_(n+1)), not A_(T_n)
formal_candidate.reinforcement_candidate: Sufficiently coherent continuation sequence may produce nondecreasing pathway bias, without a universal reinforcement claim.
formal_candidate.history_dependence: Future admissibility depends on realized continuation history encoded in present topology.
formal_candidate.non_markov_note: A complete conditioned topology may support Markov closure; a reduced state omitting relevant topology generally exhibits effective non-Markov behavior.

projection_chain: Propagation, flow, deformation, or apparent motion
Sequential change interpreted as elapsed time

asserted: Conditioned topology can alter subsequent admissibility.
Repeated coherent continuation can reinforce compatible pathways.
History can be embodied in present topology without a separate historical record.
not_asserted: Every continuation reinforces its own path.
All topology is produced solely by continuation.
Topology cannot be weakened or erased.
The mechanism is empirically validated across physical domains.

failure_modes: Circular explanation without an explicit Phi transition rule
testable_obligations: Measure repetition count against pathway bias.
Test incoherent or opposing continuation for weakening, erasure, or redirection.
Use matched present conditions with divergent prior histories.
Compare full-topology and reduced-state predictive behavior.
Test whether residue is reconstructable as present topology without a separate trace.

recommended_simulation_campaign.minimum_model: Finite basin network with typed boundaries, continuation thresholds/resistance, realized distinction conditions, topology updates, and coherent/incoherent/adversarial repetition controls.

promotion_requirements: Alignment review against residue and continuation definitions

proposed_textbook_insertion.placement_recommendation: After formal definitions of continuation, basin, boundary, and admissibility, before non-Markovian kernel treatment.

governance.supersession_policy: Later definitions of residue, continuation reinforcement, or topology update must preserve, refine, or explicitly supersede this packet by packet_id.
